stemMd: Iris: The city should publish inspection reports as soon as inspectors submit them, because residents need timely information. Leon: Reports should be published only after factual errors have been checked; a short delay is preferable to misleading residents. Their statements most clearly disagree about whether

options.label: B
options.textMd: submitted inspection reports should be published before factual checking is completed.

explanationMd: Use the yes/no test on the same proposition. Iris endorses publication on submission, before a checking delay; Leon rejects publication until checking. Their dispute is over the timing rule, not whether accuracy matters.

distractorRationale.c: Iris does not deny the value of accuracy.
distractorRationale.e: Iris expresses no view on the frequency or possibility of errors.
distractorRationale.d: Neither asserts that every delay destroys all value.
